No idea if these specific numbers generalize across tasks, but directionally it’s clear that the harness is going to become the most important variable -right next to model capability- in the AI stack. 

The ability for harnesses to break down work in the most efficient way and route to the right model at the right time is going to be a huge variable for maximizing accuracy and reducing costs.

We’re actually still incredibly early in this journey. The harness didn’t matter that much when tasks only took hundreds of thousands or millions of tokens. But as we have tasks that take tens of millions and hundreds of millions of tokens, this becomes a major variable. Huge opportunity ahead.

"Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation"

Explorative Modeling argues generative models have been missing a third scaling axis.

We scale parameters and data, but not generative expressivity, the number of modes a training objective can preserve instead of averaging into blur.

The core idea is simple. During training, generate K candidates and backprop only through the one closest to the data. This factors the training loop instead of the generation process. And that lets models commit to different modes while making generation more end-to-end.

The results are surprisingly strong too. This includes 4.1x better FLOP efficiency, 1.43 unguided ImageNet FID, 6.2x better sample efficiency, 47% better parameter efficiency across diffusion, flow, video, image, and masked diffusion LMs. 

On top of that, diffusion-level control got 16 to 256x fewer inference steps.
